Механическое удаление в репозитории LiveSpec. Рабочее дерево: `/private/tmp/ls-director/wt` (git worktree, ветка `director/2026-08-21-package-1`, чистое, синхронно с origin/main). НЕ коммить, НЕ пушить — только правки в рабочем дереве. Я проверю и закоммичу сам.

**Контекст.** Владелец дал мандат снести машинерию, которая не защищает продукт, данные, пользователя или обратимость изменений. Ниже — список проверок, чей единственный предмет — другая проверка, её реестр, её манифест, либо придуманный изнутри числовой потолок. Их надо удалить ЦЕЛИКОМ, вместе с их конфигами, манифестами, фикстурами, тестами, упоминаниями в документации и вызовами. Мёртвой совместимости оставлять нельзя.

**Удалить (каждый пункт — скрипт плюс всё, что его обслуживает):**

1. Гейт `u` — `guardrails/check-ci-mirror.sh`, данные `guardrails/ci-mirror.json`.
2. Гейт `v` — `guardrails/check-judge-listed.py`.
3. Гейт `w` — `guardrails/check-every-gate-can-fail.py`, данные `guardrails/gate-red-proofs.json`.
4. Гейт `ae` — `guardrails/check-named-checks.py`, данные `scripts/check-registry.json`.
5. Гейт `af` — `guardrails/check-gates-manifest.py`, данные `guardrails/gates-manifest.json`.
6. Гейт `ad` — `guardrails/check-tree-counts.py`, данные `guardrails/tree-counts.json`, генератор `scripts/gen-tree-counts.py`.
7. Гейт `aa` — `guardrails/check-doc-findings-bound.py`, данные `guardrails/rule-census.json`, измеритель `scripts/rule-census.py`.
8. `guardrails/check-hooks-can-fire.py`, данные `guardrails/hook-red-proofs.json`, каталог фикстур `guardrails/hook-red-fixtures/`.
9. `guardrails/node_growth_counter.py`, данные `guardrails/node-file-cap.json`.
10. `guardrails/spec-ratchet.json`.
11. `guardrails/check-suite-budget.sh` и его вызов из `guardrails/check-tests.sh` (бюджет времени прогона 1780 секунд).
12. Весь каталог `guardrails/attic/` — шесть скриптов-сирот и их фикстуры, каждый сам о себе пишет «PARKED / wired into nothing».

**НЕ трогать ничего другого.** В частности оставить полностью нетронутыми: `check-prover-record.sh` (гейт a), `check-skill-review.sh` (гейт s), `check-tests.sh` (кроме вырезания вызова бюджета), `check-matrix-reference.py`, `check-index-generated.py`, `check-prototype-fence.sh`, `check-skill-loadability.sh`, `check-shipped-language.sh`, `check-broad-kill.sh`, `check-muted-launch.sh`, `check-config-health.sh`, `check-config-health-perms.py`, `check-cleanup-notice.sh`, `check-board.py`, `check-authority-anchor.py`, `check-runaway-child.py`, `check-doc-rotation.py`, `check-agent-card.py`, `check-pin-drift.sh`, `check-freeze.sh`, `check-earned-message.py`, `check-touchpoint-kind.py`, `check-deletion-only-push.sh`, `check-push-reach.sh`, `check-future-times.sh`, `check-deferral-marker.py`, `scaffold/guardrails/*`, весь `hooks/`, `guardrails/pre-commit`, `guardrails/post-commit`.

**Порядок работы:**

**Шаг 1. Разведка перед удалением.** Для каждого удаляемого файла найди ВСЕ ссылки на него: `grep -rn "<имя-файла>" . --exclude-dir=.git` и то же по имени без расширения. Составь список мест, которые придётся править. Особое внимание: `guardrails/pre-push`, `.github/workflows/gates.yml`, `guardrails/install.sh`, `scripts/`, `tests/`, `README.md`, `guardrails/README.md`, `ARCHITECTURE.md`, `PRODUCT_SPEC.md`, тела скиллов в `skills/`.

**Шаг 2. Удаление.** `git rm -r` для файлов. Затем вычисти:
- секции соответствующих букв гейтов из `guardrails/pre-push` (там они помечены комментариями вида `-- gate X: ... --`) — удалять всю секцию буквы целиком;
- соответствующие шаги из `.github/workflows/gates.yml`;
- тесты, которые эти проверки обслуживают, — найди их по grep и удали файлы целиком, если весь файл про удаляемую проверку; если тест смешанный, удали только относящиеся тест-функции;
- упоминания в прозе документов и скиллов — удаляй предложение или строку таблицы целиком, не оставляй висящих ссылок на несуществующие файлы.

**Шаг 3. Проверка на висяки.** После удаления прогони `grep -rn` по именам всех удалённых файлов ещё раз. Ноль попаданий вне `docs/queue-archive/`, `attic/` и `.git/` (архивы трогать не надо — это замороженные исторические копии). Если попадание осталось — почини или объясни, почему оно допустимо.

**Шаг 4. Не ломай синтаксис.** После правок:
- `bash -n guardrails/pre-push` и `bash -n guardrails/check-tests.sh` — должны пройти;
- `python3 -c "import yaml,sys; yaml.safe_load(open('.github/workflows/gates.yml'))"` — должен пройти (если yaml не установлен, пропусти и скажи);
- `python3 -m pytest tests/ -q --collect-only 2>&1 | tail -5` — сбор тестов не должен падать с ошибкой импорта.

**Шаг 5. Отчёт.** Верни ОДИН документ по-русски:
- таблица: что удалено (файл) · сколько ссылок на него было · где правил;
- список файлов, которые ты правил, а не удалял, с одной фразой что именно вырезал;
- сколько букв гейтов осталось в `guardrails/pre-push` (`grep -oE -- '-- gate [a-z]{1,2}:' guardrails/pre-push | sort -u | wc -l`) и какие именно буквы;
- результат четырёх проверок Шага 4;
- всё, что осталось висеть и почему.

Не коммить. Работай через bash. Если наткнёшься на что-то, что выглядит опасным для удаления (например, файл из списка на самом деле вызывается защитой, которая остаётся) — НЕ удаляй его, оставь и напиши об этом в отчёте отдельным пунктом.

- design: Create a design canvas — a multi-artboard visual design published as an Artifact that runs Claude Design's canvas editor (an early preview of Claude Design inside Claude Code). You DRAFT the design as .dc.html artboards laid out on one pan/zoom canvas; where saving is enabled for the user's account they refine every element visually (click-to-select, a properties panel, inline text editing, undo/redo) and Save publishes a new version for everyone, otherwise they get a view-and-export (PNG/PDF) preview of your draft. Good for UI mockups and screen flows, landing pages, marketing and social graphics, and print pieces — posters, flyers, brochures as single-page artboards; memos and reports as one flowing artboard. Use when someone wants a design, mockup, wireframe, UI or screen design, landing page, poster, flyer, brochure, banner, card, one-pager, or any visual layout they would rather tweak by hand than in code. Only for CREATING or re-seeding a canvas; an existing one is edited in its published Artifact.
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- artifact-design: Design guidance and fundamentals for Artifacts. - Load before writing any artifact, including Markdown ones — format is part of the design pass, never a speed shortcut.
- artifact-diagramming: Diagramming know-how for Artifacts — when a picture earns its place, how to draw one that shows the real mechanism, and the inline-SVG mechanics that keep it legible in both themes.
- artifact-capabilities: Runtime capabilities a published Artifact page can be granted — behavior static HTML cannot provide on its own, such as the page reading live or connected data, keeping state shared across viewers, handing the viewer a file to save, or updating and republishing itself. Serves this user's live capability roster and the typed call definitions. Load it whenever the user asks for an artifact needing any such runtime behavior.
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- code-review: Review the current diff, or a PR number/branch/path target, for correctness bugs and reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings; ultra: deep multi-agent review in the cloud); with no level given, it reuses the level you typed last. Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review. For ultra on a GitHub.com PR target, --post asks to post the finished review’s findings to the PR as a single comment from the user’s GitHub account (not a review; the launch dialog still confirms in interactive sessions, while non-interactive mode posts on the flag alone) and --no-post hides that option.
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled cloud agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring cloud agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run ("run this once at 3pm", "remind me to check X tomorrow").
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).
- init: Initialize a new CLAUDE.md file with codebase documentation
- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch

This is row 420's own audit rule applied to itself — a judgment call is never a gate — and the meta-gate w would red a hollow gate that cannot fire, so shipping one would be caught anyway.      1	#!/usr/bin/env python3
     2	"""check-size-ratchet.py — the bytes-per-criterion ratchet gate (SPEC INV-264, INV-265).
     3	
     4	UNARMED until the spec-format conversion delivery (INV-270). The document is named on the command line;
     5	the recorded bound lives in `guardrails/spec-ratchet.json`.
     6	
     7	THE LAW (INV-264). The spec document records a bytes-per-criterion bound — the byte count of its
     8	criterion lines alone (glossary and preamble bytes excluded) divided by the count of criteria in its
     9	body. A delivery may lower the bound or leave it; a delivery whose new bytes-per-criterion is ABOVE the
    10	recorded bound reds. Raising the bound is a change to Requirement 280, run through the pipeline; no
    11	delivery raises it on its own (INV-265). The ratchet governs PRODUCT_SPEC.md alone.
    12	
    13	THE UNSEEDED STATE. The initial bound is the value measured at the migration-end freeze, recorded by
    14	the freeze actor (INV-264 criterion 3). Before that freeze the spec is not yet in the requirements
    15	format, so `bytes_per_criterion` is null: the gate reads it as "not yet seeded" and PASSES with the
    16	config's stated reason rather than red-ing on an absent bound. This gate never writes the config —
    17	seeding and lowering the recorded bound are the freeze actor's step, not a side effect of a check.
    18	
    19	Usage:
    20	  check-size-ratchet.py <document.md> [<part.md> ...]
    21	  RATCHET_CONFIG overrides the config path (the suite points it at a fixture bound).
    22	Exit 0 when the bound is unseeded, or the new bytes-per-criterion is at or below it (printing the reach
    23	line, INV-269); exit 1 when it is above. Stdlib only.
    24	"""
    25	import json
    26	import os
    27	import sys
    28	
    29	SCRIPT_DIR = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
    30	sys.path.insert(0, SCRIPT_DIR)
    31	import specformat as sf  # noqa: E402
    32	from nonempty_input import require_nonempty, VacuousInputError  # noqa: E402
    33	
    34	CHECK = "check-size-ratchet"
    35	CONFIG_PATH = os.environ.get("RATCHET_CONFIG", os.path.join(SCRIPT_DIR, "spec-ratchet.json"))
    36	
    37	
    38	def bytes_per_criterion(doc):
    39	    """The byte count of the document's criterion lines alone, divided by the count of criteria."""
    40	    crits = doc.criteria
    41	    total = sum(sf.criterion_bytes(c.text) for c in crits)
    42	    return total, len(crits)
    43	
    44	
    45	def main(argv):
    46	    if len(argv) < 2:
    47	        print("%s: usage: %s <document.md> [<part.md> ...]" % (CHECK, os.path.basename(argv[0])))
    48	        return 2
    49	    # The document may arrive as a core plus its parts (specformat's parts map). The ratchet measures
    50	    # the whole document, so it reads the concatenation; with no parts this is the single file.
    51	    paths = sf.spec_paths(argv[1:])
    52	    missing = [p for p in paths if not os.path.isfile(p)]
    53	    if missing:
    54	        print("%s: cannot read %s — the gate stands on the document file."
    55	              % (CHECK, ", ".join(missing)))
    56	        return 1
    57	    names = [os.path.basename(p) for p in paths]
    58	    _read, text = sf.read_document(paths, expand=False)
    59	    doc = sf.parse(text)
    60

def test_one_record_and_one_gate_carry_the_push_review():
    """The merge itself: the push chain runs one review-record gate over one record home. The
    second gate, its record home and its registry entry are gone, and the retired script rests
    in the attic under its manifest line."""
    prepush = read("guardrails/pre-push")
    assert "check-prover-record.sh" in prepush, "pre-push does not wire the review-record gate"
    assert "-- gate a:" in prepush, "the review-record gate carries no gate letter in pre-push"
    assert "check-push-review" not in prepush, "the second review gate is still wired into pre-push"

    assert not os.path.exists(os.path.join(ROOT, "guardrails", "check-push-review.sh")), \
        "the retired second gate still ships under guardrails/"
    assert os.path.isfile(os.path.join(ROOT, "attic", "check-push-review.sh")), \
        "the retired second gate does not rest in the attic"
    assert "check-push-review.sh" in read("attic/MANIFEST.md"), \
        "the retired second gate carries no attic manifest line"

    assert not os.path.isdir(os.path.join(ROOT, "docs", "push-review")), \
        "the second record home still stands"

    with open(os.path.join(ROOT, "guardrails", "gate-red-proofs.json"), encoding="utf-8") as f:
        reg = json.load(f)
    assert "ac" not in reg["proofs"], "the retired gate still holds a known-red proof entry"

## Requirement 1: The spec keeps what is built apart from what is planned

**Context:** The spec states what is built and working today apart from what is only planned, and it keeps a reader from mistaking one for the other. A planned feature carries the target tag on a line of its own, and the tag never spreads to the section around it. The suite ties each target tag to the queue row that builds it — a row still open, awaiting its landing — so the marker is enforced by the suite.

**User Story:** As a reader of the spec, I want a planned feature marked by a target tag the suite enforces, so that I never mistake a promised surface for a working one.

### Acceptance Criteria

**Case: built and planned are marked apart**

1. The spec *shall* state what is built and working today apart from what is only planned, marking each scenario and its named promised parts apart, so a scenario that holds built parts beside planned ones states a status for the scenario and for every named promised part. [S-0]
2. The system *shall* carry the target tag on a line of its own and *shall* keep it off the section around it. [S-0]

**Case: the suite ties each tag to its building row**

...

## Requirement 246: The guards over the guards

**Context:** A gate can report green two ways: because the input was clean, or because it never fires at all. Four checks guard the gate machinery itself against that hollow class — the pushed gates must be mirrored into the remote check, every chat judge the pack declares wired must be wired into settings, every gate must carry a proof it can fail, and every path a permission rule names must still exist.

**User Story:** As a maintainer trusting the push gate, I want the gate machinery itself checked, so that no gate silently protects nothing — mirrored into the remote, wired into settings where the declaration says wired, provably able to fail, and pointed at real paths.

### Acceptance Criteria

**Case: the remote mirror carries every local gate**

1. *when* the push gate runs a gate letter locally that the remote mirror does not run, the system *shall* red, naming the gate and the one fix, a legitimate remote-skip living in `guardrails/ci-mirror.json` with its reason. [INV-210, M-5]
2. *if* a carve-out names a letter that is no local gate, *then* the system *shall* red it as drift. [INV-210]

**Case: every chat judge the declaration wires is wired**

3. *when* a hook under `hooks/` is not classified in the wired-hook declaration, or a wired hook is missing from its array in the installed settings, the system *shall* red, naming the hook, the surface, and the fix. [INV-211]
4. *where* the personal-layer settings cannot be read, the system *shall* stand the wiring check down by name rather than falsely pass. [INV-211, INV-175]

**Case: every gate carries a known-red proof**

## Requirement 280: A document's bytes-per-criterion may only fall

**Context:** The spec grows one delivery at a time, and prose can bloat while the rule count holds. To hold the density, the spec document records a bytes-per-criterion bound — its size ratchet — and the ratchet gate holds that bound. A delivery may push the bound down or leave it, and may not push it up; raising the bound is itself a change to this requirement and takes the same route through the pipeline. The ratchet governs the spec document alone, and the other documents keep their flat byte bound.

**User Story:** As a person who owns the spec's readability over time, I want the spec document's bytes-per-criterion bound to move only down, so that no single delivery is free to bloat the prose.

### Acceptance Criteria

**Case: the recorded bound**

1. The spec document `PRODUCT_SPEC.md` *shall* record a bytes-per-criterion bound, measured as the byte count of its criterion lines alone — glossary and preamble bytes excluded — divided by the count of criteria in its body. [INV-264]
2. The recorded bound *shall* live in the file `guardrails/spec-ratchet.json`. [INV-264]
3. The initial bound *shall* be the value measured at the migration-end freeze, recorded by the freeze actor. [INV-264]
4. The ratchet *shall* govern `PRODUCT_SPEC.md` only; `ROADMAP.md`, `TEST_MATRIX.md`, and `JOURNAL.md` *shall* keep their flat document byte bound. [INV-264]

**Case: the ratchet moves only down**

5. *when* a delivery freezes the spec document, the system *shall* compute the new bytes-per-criterion and *shall* require it to be at or below the recorded bound. [INV-264]

## Requirement 168: The version-control gate runs before the first delivery

**Context:** Every host reaches its first delivery through the same gate, and both a fresh start and an attach run it in the same order. A gate cannot protect files older than itself, so the gate runs before anything is created or moved. The gate settles two things: that git exists, and that a remote either exists or is declined on the record.

**User Story:** As a person starting or attaching a host, I want the version-control gate settled before the first delivery, so that no work is committed somewhere it cannot be recovered or tracked.

### Acceptance Criteria

## Requirement 246: The guards over the guards

**Context:** A gate can report green two ways: because the input was clean, or because it never fires at all. Four checks guard the gate machinery itself against that hollow class — the pushed gates must be mirrored into the remote check, every chat judge the pack declares wired must be wired into settings, every gate must carry a proof it can fail, and every path a permission rule names must still exist.

**User Story:** As a maintainer trusting the push gate, I want the gate machinery itself checked, so that no gate silently protects nothing — mirrored into the remote, wired into settings where the declaration says wired, provably able to fail, and pointed at real paths.

**Context:** The spec grows one delivery at a time, and prose can bloat while the rule count holds. To hold the density, the spec document records a bytes-per-criterion bound — its size ratchet — and the ratchet gate holds that bound. A delivery may push the bound down or leave it, and may not push it up; raising the bound is itself a change to this requirement and takes the same route through the pipeline. The ratchet governs the spec document alone, and the other documents keep their flat byte bound.

=== tests/test_description_field.py ===
     275 tests/test_description_field.py
"""The Formal-index non-empty description-field gate (SPEC INV-239, M-421; E-35/INV-239, M-423).

The named-reference pair gives every registered code a plain one-sentence description, and that
description's one home is a dedicated field the Formal index gains [E-35, base rule 4]. This suite
covers the mechanical presence net over that field — `guardrails/attic/check-description-field.py` — and
the field's own existence in the shipped index.

Two facts sit under one owning test file, as the matrix rows say (M-421 the gate, M-423 the field):
the gate reds a registered code whose description field is empty and passes one that carries a
description, judging PRESENCE alone and never whether the description reads well or matches the item
(that semantic read is the human sampling net, INV-41); and it ships DORMANT — the existing code set
carries no rich descriptions yet (the back-describe migration is a future his-gated landing, INV-217,
folded finding N5), so an armed gate would red the whole tree, and the gate stays down until the
migration arms it through `guardrails/attic/description-field.json`.

Every armed/dormant case drives the real shipped script over a FIXTURE Formal-index snippet and a
FIXTURE config, so the real `guardrails/attic/description-field.json` is never flipped and the real tree
stays green under the dormant ship.
"""
import json
import os
import re
import subprocess
import tempfile
import unittest

=== tests/test_far_tier.py ===
     155 tests/test_far_tier.py
"""The queue has a far tier, and it stands down by name and surfaces itself rarely.

SPEC INV-222 (ROADMAP 382) — a wish kept because discarding it would lose the thought, carrying
no revisit trigger and no plan to run, takes the `far` status, distinct from `deferred` whose
trigger the queue-take re-scans every time [INV-129]; the what's-left report and the feature map
read the runnable queue and stand the far tier down by name, offering it on request.

SPEC INV-223 (ROADMAP 403) — the far backlog surfaces itself rarely and unasked: the status
report carries a rare line naming that a far tier exists, at a settings-ladder cadence default
(at most once every fourteen days) with a dated marker; a second offer inside the window reds.

The checker `guardrails/attic/check-far-tier.py` is report-shape only and is NOT in the pre-push
chain (a chat report is not a committed file a push gate could scan); the suite drives it over
fixtures. It was parked in the attic on 2026-08-18 with those fixtures beside it, having never
been wired anywhere and never caught a real defect; this suite still drives it there.
"""
import os
import subprocess

from conftest import ROOT, read, read_all, read_all_flat

CHECK = os.path.join(ROOT, "guardrails", "attic", "check-far-tier.py")
FIX = os.path.join(ROOT, "guardrails", "attic", "far-tier-fixtures")



=== tests/test_vacuous_pass.py ===
     221 tests/test_vacuous_pass.py
"""INV-218 (M-399, ROADMAP 384) — a check that looked at nothing is not a pass.

The vacuous-pass class: a check whose INPUT SET is empty reports clean while testing
nothing, and an empty input set is nearly always the defect. The drafter's own self-catch
minted this row — it scanned its freshly minted codes for collisions, the codes were absent
from the prose entirely, and the scan compared zero against zero and reported clean.

The law (sibling of the unexpected-skip law INV-155): a check DECLARES the input set it
expects to be non-empty, and an empty set REDS BY NAME rather than passing silently. This
movement builds the shared shape (`guardrails/nonempty_input.py`) and applies it to the first
named instance — the traceability index prose check `guardrails/attic/check-index-prose.py`, which
today has no home for the "a Formal-index code whose home prose never carries the anchor"
defect: `test_spec_index_unique_anchors` checks uniqueness alone.

Every check here asserts the SHIPPED files on disk, never a source fragment or a memory of one.
"""
import os
import re
import subprocess
import sys
import tempfile
import unittest

# The suite's one reading node: for the spec it returns the core and every part the map
# names, and for any other file the file itself. A local reader would have shadowed it.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""route_agent_transport.py — which transport carries a message between two agents (SPEC INV-236, ROADMAP 396).

INV-183's transport sentence was written on a refused premise: that git is the universal transport
for all inter-agent traffic and co-location only a fast path. The owner refused it 2026-07-17. The
cut runs by the traffic's KIND, not by where the two agents sit:

- A message needing no timely answer — a durable record a neighbour reads on its own clock, or a
  notification — travels by the STORE: the sender deposits one new file and the receiver sweeps it
  later, reachable while the receiver is not running and committed-and-pushed when the sender is
  remote [INV-112]. This road works today; the remote-deposit arm landed [ROADMAP 247].

- A conversation — a back-and-forth needing a live peer that answers in turn — needs a DIRECT
  CHANNEL, and the harness has not shipped one: the socket plumbing is built and switched off, no
  listener has shipped, so two local sessions have no live direct channel today.

The conversation road's availability is FIELD-GATED on the same machine-fact the listener tripwire
reads [INV-231]: a session record carrying a non-empty socket field is a listener. Today's
listenerless harness leaves the direct channel unavailable. The availability is read from the
session records, never hardcoded, so the day a listener ships the road flips to available on its
own — that day being row 405's mechanical tripwire.

WHERE IT LIVES. Like the listener tripwire, this rides the suite and takes NO push-gate letter: a
router is a stated routing rule a test exercises, not a committed file a push gate scans [INV-83].
"""
import importlib.util
import os

_HERE = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))

# The traffic kinds. A conversation needs a live peer answering in turn; a no-answer message needs
# no timely reply — a durable record or a notification the receiver reads on its own clock.
_CONVERSATION_KINDS = ("conversation", "dialogue", "live-exchange")
_NO_ANSWER_KINDS = ("record", "notification", "deposit", "no-answer")


def _listener_module():
    """The listener tripwire's single source of the socket-field truth, loaded by path.

    Reusing it keeps ONE home for what counts as a shipped listener [INV-194], so the router and
    the tripwire never drift on the machine-fact they both read. The tripwire moved to
    `guardrails/attic/` on 2026-08-18; the router still reads it there, so the one home holds.
    """
    path = os.path.join(_HERE, "attic", "check-listener-tripwire.py")
    spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location("check_listener_tripwire", path)
    mod = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec)
    spec.loader.exec_module(mod)
    return mod


def classify(message):
    """The message's traffic kind: 'conversation', 'no-answer', or None when it declares neither.

    A message declares its kind through a `kind` field (a conversation, or a no-answer
    record/notification) or a `needs_answer` boolean. A message stating neither is unclassified;
    the router refuses it rather than guessing [INV-4].
    """
    if not isinstance(message, dict):
        return None
    kind = message.get("kind")
    if kind in _CONVERSATION_KINDS:
        return "conversation"
    if kind in _NO_ANSWER_KINDS:
        return "no-answer"
    na = message.get("needs_answer")
    if na is True:
        return "conversation"
    if na is False:
        return "no-answer"
    return None

Beside its concrete layers and proofs (INV-135), its design principles (INV-136) and its composition
axes (INV-244), a project kind whose product is deployed carries one more founding declaration: the
seam between what ships inside a build and what the owner turns from outside it. An experiment switch,
a piece of copy, a threshold or budget, and a feature toggle live on the configuration side and reach
production by a deploy of configuration alone; behaviour and structure stay in the code the build
ships. The founding records that seam on a `project.config-surface` line in the host profile, and the
check `guardrails/check-config-surface.py` reds a profile that records a kind and declares no such
surface.

Two things this file proves, kept distinct:

  1. The check itself — a runnable gate over a host profile, driven here by subprocess on fixture
     profiles. It reds on silence, passes on an explicit "none" from a project that deploys nothing,
     and reds a "none" that contradicts the host's own declared deployment layer. It rides the suite
     and stays off the push chain, the standing `guardrails/attic/check-wrong-referral.py` already carries
     [INV-225], because the pack ships no deployed product of its own.

     node's owns cell, the matrix row, the versioned founding-question set, adoption's orient, and the
     pack's own host profile. The document homes land in the fenced core documents, so the tests
     pointing at them stay red until those blocks are applied.
"""

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
2	# pre-push — the live-spec push gate (SPEC M-6; scope grown by prover findings F7/F4;
3	# gate e added for INV-17, the prototype fence).
4	# Blocks a push unless every gate below passes.
5	#
6	# Generic pattern for a host project: copy this file, then in guardrails/README.md's
7	# "how a host adapts" section swap in your own test command and prover cadence — the
8	# gate shape (fresh review record / green tests / ownership / coverage) travels as-is.
9	
10	set -euo pipefail
11	
12	REPO_ROOT="$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)"
13	cd "$REPO_ROOT"
14	GUARDRAILS="$REPO_ROOT/guardrails"
15	
16	# -- deletion-only stand-down (SPEC INV-290, ROADMAP row 502) --
17	# git feeds this hook one ref-update line per pushed ref on stdin (githooks(5)); read it ONCE, here,
18	# before any gate below can touch stdin — a manual invocation for testing leaves stdin as a tty and
19	# must never block on a read. A push whose every fed line deletes its remote counterpart (the
20	# all-zero local object id) carries no content for any gate to judge, so the whole chain stands down
21	# by name instead of falling to the reach map's conservative FULL — the fix for the 2026-07-27 hang
22	# (four tag deletions read as an empty diff, fell to the full suite, died on the two-minute limit).
23	# This check carries no gate letter: it is a triage read ahead of the chain, the placement
24	# check-push-reach.sh already holds inside gate b, not a net that blocks on red.
25	#
26	# The marker below is the machine-readable half of the convention guardrails/check-prover-record.sh
27	# states in full: every arm that can let a push past the prover-record demand carries one
28	# `# STAND-DOWN: <name>` line, and PRODUCT_SPEC.md R226 criterion 6 must name that same <name>.
29	# tests/test_deletion_only_push.py reads both directions off these markers.
30	# STAND-DOWN: deletion-only
31	if [ -t 0 ]; then
32	  PUSH_REF_LINES=""
33	else
34	  PUSH_REF_LINES="$(cat)"
35	fi
36	export PUSH_REF_LINES
37	if [ -n "$PUSH_REF_LINES" ]; then
38	  set +e
39	  del_out="$("$GUARDRAILS/check-deletion-only-push.sh")"
40	  del_code=$?
41	  set -e
42	  if [ "$del_code" -eq 0 ]; then
43	    echo "$del_out"
44	    echo "PUSH ALLOWED — deletion-only push: standing the full gate chain down (reason: a deletion carries no content for any gate to judge, SPEC INV-290); whatever would guard the deletion itself is unaffected, since no such gate exists in this chain today."
45	    exit 0
46	  fi
47	fi
48	
49	fail=0
50	
51	# -- the fast local chain (2026-08-18) --
52	# The local chain runs the checks that take seconds: the prover record, the pins, skill
53	# loadability, and the registry and accounting checks. The one slow member is gate b, the whole
54	# pytest suite, which takes over twenty minutes on this machine and is the SERVER's job — the
55	# gates workflow runs `python3 -m pytest -q` on every push, in the step named
56	# "test suite (gate b, full — the reach map stays local)" (.github/workflows/gates.yml). Running
57	# it a second time on the pusher's machine bought a slower push, not a safer one.
58	# The old chain is still here and still reachable: LIVE_SPEC_PUSH_FULL=1 runs gate b locally
59	# exactly as before, reach-scoped, with its suite-budget arm. That is the flag for a machine with
60	# no server, a network-less push, or anyone who wants the old behaviour.
61	# Nothing else moved: every gate whose value is catching something BEFORE the push — gate a's
62	# fresh prover record above all — runs on every push as it always did.
63	PUSH_FULL="${LIVE_SPEC_PUSH_FULL:-}"
64	
65	# Gate g, pin drift, is the second cost in the local chain: 56 seconds on 2026-08-18, more than
66	# every other fast gate together. It stays — it holds pins repaired BEFORE a push, and it proved
67	# sixty-odd re-aimed pins the evening before — but it stops charging a push that cannot have moved
68	# a pin. A pin lives in ARCHITECTURE.md or in the r5 rule-price page, and points at a file. So a
69	# diff touching none of: ARCHITECTURE.md, .live-spec/r5-rule-prices-2026-08-11.md, skills/ (the r5
70	# page pins skill rules), the gate's own two readers, or any file an ARCHITECTURE.md pin names,
71	# cannot have moved one.
72	# The diff base is the chain's own, LIVE_SPEC_DIFF_BASE with origin/main as the default, the base
73	# gate a and the reach classifier already read. Every unreadable answer runs the gate: no base, no
74	# diff, no pin list. The SERVER runs gate g unconditionally (.github/workflows/gates.yml), so the
75	# guarantee is unchanged — it just stops being paid for on every push that cannot touch it.
76	# PIN_REACH_FILES replaces the diff for tests only, the way REACH_FILES does in check-push-reach.sh.
77	gate_g_can_skip() {
78	  # exit 0 = this diff cannot have moved a pin, gate g may stand down; 1 = run it.
79	  local base changed targets f
80	  [ -n "$PUSH_FULL" ] && return 1
81	  if [ -n "${PIN_REACH_FILES:-}" ]; then
82	    changed="$PIN_REACH_FILES"
83	  else
84	    base="${LIVE_SPEC_DIFF_BASE:-origin/main}"
85	    git rev-parse --verify --quiet "$base" >/dev/null || return 1
86	    changed="$(git diff --name-only "$base"..HEAD || true)"
87	  fi
88	  [ -z "$changed" ] && return 1
89	  targets="$(python3 "$GUARDRAILS/archformat.py" --pins "$REPO_ROOT/ARCHITECTURE.md" 2>/dev/null | cut -f1 | sort -u || true)"
90	  [ -z "$targets" ] && return 1
91	  while IFS= read -r f; do
92	    [ -z "$f" ] && continue
93	    case "$f" in
94	      ARCHITECTURE.md|.live-spec/r5-rule-prices-2026-08-11.md|skills/*) return 1 ;;
95	      guardrails/check-pin-drift.sh|guardrails/archformat.py) return 1 ;;  # the gate's own reading changed
96	    esac
97	    if printf '%s\n' "$targets" | grep -qxF -- "$f"; then
98	      return 1
99	    fi
100	  done <<< "$changed"
101	  return 0
102	}
103	
104	echo "== live-spec push gate =="
105	
106	echo ""
107	echo "-- reach classification (one read, feeds gates a and b, SPEC INV-45) --"
108	set +e
109	reach_out="$("$GUARDRAILS/check-push-reach.sh")"
110	reach_code=$?
111	set -e
112	echo "$reach_out"
113	
114	echo ""
115	echo "-- gate a: fresh prover record for today (one record per push: the re-check of the spec and the architecture, and the adversarial read of the pushed range, SPEC M-6/INV-116/INV-304) --"
116	# The reach verdict does not scope this gate (the 2718c69 stand-down, reverted on the owner's
117	# 2026-08-15 word). A prose-only or scoped diff still sends commits, and the record this gate
118	# demands is the adversarial read of the pushed RANGE (INV-304) — a thing no file-class verdict
119	# can stand down for. The only stand-downs that exist are the two PRODUCT_SPEC.md R226.6 names
120	# by hand: a deletion-only push (handled above, before this chain) and the recordless class.
121	if ! "$GUARDRAILS/check-prover-record.sh" --push; then
122	  fail=1
123	fi
124	
125	echo ""
126	echo "-- gate b: test suite green (scoped by the diff's reach, SPEC INV-45) --"
127	if [ -z "$PUSH_FULL" ]; then
128	  echo "   the server runs this one: .github/workflows/gates.yml runs python3 -m pytest -q on every"
129	  echo "   push, in its step \"test suite (gate b, full — the reach map stays local)\". The local"
130	  echo "   chain is the fast set, so a push here does not pay the suite's twenty minutes twice."
131	  echo "   Run it locally with LIVE_SPEC_PUSH_FULL=1 git push, or python3 -m pytest -q by hand."
132	else
133	  echo "   LIVE_SPEC_PUSH_FULL is set: running the suite locally, reach-scoped, as the chain always did."
134	  case "$reach_code" in
135	    0)
136	      echo "   prose-only diff: the suite stands down by name; every other gate still runs."
137	      ;;
138	    2)
139	      scoped_files="$(printf '%s\n' "$reach_out" | sed -n 's/^SCOPED //p')"
140	      if ! SCOPED_TEST_FILES="$scoped_files" "$GUARDRAILS/check-tests.sh"; then
141	        fail=1
142	      fi
143	      ;;
144	    *)
145	      if ! "$GUARDRAILS/check-tests.sh"; then
146	        fail=1
147	      fi
148	      ;;
149	  esac
150	fi
151	
152	echo ""
153	echo "-- gate c: every spec anchor owned by exactly one architecture node --"
154	echo "   Covered by gate b: tests/test_traceability.py already asserts this"
155	echo "   (test_architecture_owns_every_anchor_once) — no separate check needed here."
156	
157	echo ""
158	echo "-- gate d: TEST_MATRIX.md generated Reference agrees with the body (SPEC INV-273/INV-218) --"
159	if ! python3 "$GUARDRAILS/check-matrix-reference.py" "$REPO_ROOT/TEST_MATRIX.md" "$REPO_ROOT/TEST_MATRIX.index.md"; then
160	  fail=1
161	fi
162	
163	echo ""
164	echo "-- gate g: pin drift --"
165	if gate_g_can_skip; then
166	  echo "   the diff touches no pin: it changes neither ARCHITECTURE.md, nor the r5 rule-price page,"
167	  echo "   nor skills/, nor any file a pin names, so nothing in it can have moved a pin. The server"
168	  echo "   runs gate g on every push (.github/workflows/gates.yml), and LIVE_SPEC_PUSH_FULL=1 runs it here."
169	else
170	  if ! "$GUARDRAILS/check-pin-drift.sh"; then
171	    fail=1
172	  fi
173	fi
174	
175	echo "-- gate f: skill loadability --"
176	if ! "$GUARDRAILS/check-skill-loadability.sh"; then
177	  fail=1
178	fi
179	
180	echo "-- gate e: prototype fence --"
181	if ! "$GUARDRAILS/check-prototype-fence.sh"; then
182	  fail=1
183	fi
184	
185	echo "-- gate i: shipped-language (no owner name or stray Cyrillic in the shipped set, SPEC INV-120) --"
186	if ! "$GUARDRAILS/check-shipped-language.sh"; then
187	  fail=1
188	fi
189	
190	echo ""
191	echo "-- gate j: no broad browser-kill (cleanup targets the test resource only, SPEC INV-162) --"
192	if ! "$GUARDRAILS/check-broad-kill.sh"; then
193	  fail=1
194	fi
195	
196	echo ""
197	echo "-- gate l: muted browser launch (every browser-driving script launches muted, SPEC INV-157) --"
198	if ! "$GUARDRAILS/check-muted-launch.sh"; then
199	  fail=1
200	fi
201	
202	echo ""
203	echo "-- gate o: cleanup notice (every cleanup path that ends a process says what it ended, SPEC INV-204) --"
204	if ! "$GUARDRAILS/check-cleanup-notice.sh"; then
205	  fail=1
206	fi

210	if ! python3 "$GUARDRAILS/check-touchpoint-kind.py"; then
211	  fail=1
212	fi

216	if ! python3 "$GUARDRAILS/check-board.py"; then
217	  fail=1

222	if ! python3 "$GUARDRAILS/check-authority-anchor.py"; then
223	  fail=1

228	if ! "$GUARDRAILS/check-skill-review.sh"; then

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# pre-push — the live-spec push gate (SPEC M-6; scope grown by prover findings F7/F4;
# gate e added for INV-17, the prototype fence).
# Blocks a push unless every gate below passes.
#
# Generic pattern for a host project: copy this file, then in guardrails/README.md's
# "how a host adapts" section swap in your own test command and prover cadence — the
# gate shape (fresh review record / green tests / ownership / coverage) travels as-is.

set -euo pipefail

REPO_ROOT="$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)"
cd "$REPO_ROOT"
GUARDRAILS="$REPO_ROOT/guardrails"

# -- deletion-only stand-down (SPEC INV-290, ROADMAP row 502) --
# git feeds this hook one ref-update line per pushed ref on stdin (githooks(5)); read it ONCE, here,
# before any gate below can touch stdin — a manual invocation for testing leaves stdin as a tty and
# must never block on a read. A push whose every fed line deletes its remote counterpart (the
# all-zero local object id) carries no content for any gate to judge, so the whole chain stands down
# by name instead of falling to the reach map's conservative FULL — the fix for the 2026-07-27 hang
# (four tag deletions read as an empty diff, fell to the full suite, died on the two-minute limit).
# This check carries no gate letter: it is a triage read ahead of the chain, the placement
# check-push-reach.sh already holds inside gate b, not a net that blocks on red.
#
# The marker below is the machine-readable half of the convention guardrails/check-prover-record.sh
# states in full: every arm that can let a push past the prover-record demand carries one
# `# STAND-DOWN: <name>` line, and PRODUCT_SPEC.md R226 criterion 6 must name that same <name>.
# tests/test_deletion_only_push.py reads both directions off these markers.
# STAND-DOWN: deletion-only
if [ -t 0 ]; then
  PUSH_REF_LINES=""
else
  PUSH_REF_LINES="$(cat)"
fi
export PUSH_REF_LINES
if [ -n "$PUSH_REF_LINES" ]; then
  set +e
  del_out="$("$GUARDRAILS/check-deletion-only-push.sh")"
  del_code=$?
  set -e
  if [ "$del_code" -eq 0 ]; then
    echo "$del_out"
    echo "PUSH ALLOWED — deletion-only push: standing the full gate chain down (reason: a deletion carries no content for any gate to judge, SPEC INV-290); whatever would guard the deletion itself is unaffected, since no such gate exists in this chain today."
    exit 0
  fi
fi

fail=0

# -- the fast local chain (2026-08-18) --
# The local chain runs the checks that take seconds: the prover record, the pins, skill
# loadability, and the registry and accounting checks. The one slow member is gate b, the whole
# pytest suite, which takes over twenty minutes on this machine and is the SERVER's job — the
# gates workflow runs `python3 -m pytest -q` on every push, in the step named
# "test suite (gate b, full — the reach map stays local)" (.github/workflows/gates.yml). Running
# it a second time on the pusher's machine bought a slower push, not a safer one.
# The old chain is still here and still reachable: LIVE_SPEC_PUSH_FULL=1 runs gate b locally
# exactly as before, reach-scoped, with its suite-budget arm. That is the flag for a machine with
# no server, a network-less push, or anyone who wants the old behaviour.
# Nothing else moved: every gate whose value is catching something BEFORE the push — gate a's
# fresh prover record above all — runs on every push as it always did.
PUSH_FULL="${LIVE_SPEC_PUSH_FULL:-}"

# Gate g, pin drift, is the second cost in the local chain: 56 seconds on 2026-08-18, more than
# every other fast gate together. It stays — it holds pins repaired BEFORE a push, and it proved
# sixty-odd re-aimed pins the evening before — but it stops charging a push that cannot have moved
# a pin. A pin lives in ARCHITECTURE.md or in the r5 rule-price page, and points at a file. So a
# diff touching none of: ARCHITECTURE.md, .live-spec/r5-rule-prices-2026-08-11.md, skills/ (the r5
# page pins skill rules), the gate's own two readers, or any file an ARCHITECTURE.md pin names,
# cannot have moved one.
# The diff base is the chain's own, LIVE_SPEC_DIFF_BASE with origin/main as the default, the base
# gate a and the reach classifier already read. Every unreadable answer runs the gate: no base, no
# diff, no pin list. The SERVER runs gate g unconditionally (.github/workflows/gates.yml), so the
# guarantee is unchanged — it just stops being paid for on every push that cannot touch it.
# PIN_REACH_FILES replaces the diff for tests only, the way REACH_FILES does in check-push-reach.sh.
gate_g_can_skip() {
  # exit 0 = this diff cannot have moved a pin, gate g may stand down; 1 = run it.
  local base changed targets f
  [ -n "$PUSH_FULL" ] && return 1
  if [ -n "${PIN_REACH_FILES:-}" ]; then
    changed="$PIN_REACH_FILES"
  else
    base="${LIVE_SPEC_DIFF_BASE:-origin/main}"
    git rev-parse --verify --quiet "$base" >/dev/null || return 1
    changed="$(git diff --name-only "$base"..HEAD || true)"
  fi
  [ -z "$changed" ] && return 1
  targets="$(python3 "$GUARDRAILS/archformat.py" --pins "$REPO_ROOT/ARCHITECTURE.md" 2>/dev/null | cut -f1 | sort -u || true)"
  [ -z "$targets" ] && return 1
  while IFS= read -r f; do
    [ -z "$f" ] && continue
    case "$f" in
      ARCHITECTURE.md|.live-spec/r5-rule-prices-2026-08-11.md|skills/*) return 1 ;;
      guardrails/check-pin-drift.sh|guardrails/archformat.py) return 1 ;;  # the gate's own reading changed
    esac
    if printf '%s\n' "$targets" | grep -qxF -- "$f"; then
      return 1
    fi
  done <<< "$changed"
  return 0
}

echo "== live-spec push gate =="

echo ""
echo "-- reach classification (one read, feeds gates a and b, SPEC INV-45) --"
set +e
reach_out="$("$GUARDRAILS/check-push-reach.sh")"
reach_code=$?
set -e
echo "$reach_out"

echo ""
echo "-- gate a: fresh prover record for today (one record per push: the re-check of the spec and the architecture, and the adversarial read of the pushed range, SPEC M-6/INV-116/INV-304) --"
# The reach verdict does not scope this gate (the 2718c69 stand-down, reverted on the owner's
# 2026-08-15 word). A prose-only or scoped diff still sends commits, and the record this gate
# demands is the adversarial read of the pushed RANGE (INV-304) — a thing no file-class verdict
# can stand down for. The only stand-downs that exist are the two PRODUCT_SPEC.md R226.6 names
# by hand: a deletion-only push (handled above, before this chain) and the recordless class.
if ! "$GUARDRAILS/check-prover-record.sh" --push; then
  fail=1
fi

echo ""
echo "-- gate b: test suite green (scoped by the diff's reach, SPEC INV-45) --"
if [ -z "$PUSH_FULL" ]; then
  echo "   the server runs this one: .github/workflows/gates.yml runs python3 -m pytest -q on every"
  echo "   push, in its step \"test suite (gate b, full — the reach map stays local)\". The local"
  echo "   chain is the fast set, so a push here does not pay the suite's twenty minutes twice."
  echo "   Run it locally with LIVE_SPEC_PUSH_FULL=1 git push, or python3 -m pytest -q by hand."
else
  echo "   LIVE_SPEC_PUSH_FULL is set: running the suite locally, reach-scoped, as the chain always did."
  case "$reach_code" in
    0)
      echo "   prose-only diff: the suite stands down by name; every other gate still runs."
      ;;
    2)
      scoped_files="$(printf '%s\n' "$reach_out" | sed -n 's/^SCOPED //p')"
      if ! SCOPED_TEST_FILES="$scoped_files" "$GUARDRAILS/check-tests.sh"; then
        fail=1
      fi
      ;;
    *)
      if ! "$GUARDRAILS/check-tests.sh"; then
        fail=1
      fi
      ;;
  esac
fi

echo ""
echo "-- gate c: every spec anchor owned by exactly one architecture node --"
echo "   Covered by gate b: tests/test_traceability.py already asserts this"
echo "   (test_architecture_owns_every_anchor_once) — no separate check needed here."

echo ""
echo "-- gate d: TEST_MATRIX.md generated Reference agrees with the body (SPEC INV-273/INV-218) --"
if ! python3 "$GUARDRAILS/check-matrix-reference.py" "$REPO_ROOT/TEST_MATRIX.md" "$REPO_ROOT/TEST_MATRIX.index.md"; then
  fail=1
fi

echo ""
echo "-- gate g: pin drift --"
if gate_g_can_skip; then
  echo "   the diff touches no pin: it changes neither ARCHITECTURE.md, nor the r5 rule-price page,"
  echo "   nor skills/, nor any file a pin names, so nothing in it can have moved a pin. The server"
  echo "   runs gate g on every push (.github/workflows/gates.yml), and LIVE_SPEC_PUSH_FULL=1 runs it here."
else
  if ! "$GUARDRAILS/check-pin-drift.sh"; then
    fail=1
  fi
fi

echo "-- gate f: skill loadability --"
if ! "$GUARDRAILS/check-skill-loadability.sh"; then
  fail=1
fi

echo "-- gate e: prototype fence --"
if ! "$GUARDRAILS/check-prototype-fence.sh"; then
  fail=1
fi

echo "-- gate i: shipped-language (no owner name or stray Cyrillic in the shipped set, SPEC INV-120) --"
if ! "$GUARDRAILS/check-shipped-language.sh"; then
  fail=1
fi

echo ""
echo "-- gate j: no broad browser-kill (cleanup targets the test resource only, SPEC INV-162) --"
if ! "$GUARDRAILS/check-broad-kill.sh"; then
  fail=1
fi

echo ""
echo "-- gate l: muted browser launch (every browser-driving script launches muted, SPEC INV-157) --"
if ! "$GUARDRAILS/check-muted-launch.sh"; then
  fail=1
fi

echo ""
echo "-- gate o: cleanup notice (every cleanup path that ends a process says what it ended, SPEC INV-204) --"
if ! "$GUARDRAILS/check-cleanup-notice.sh"; then
  fail=1
fi

echo ""
echo "-- gate p: touchpoint kind (a surface speaks only the kind its touchpoint affords, SPEC INV-205) --"
if ! python3 "$GUARDRAILS/check-touchpoint-kind.py"; then
  fail=1
fi

echo ""
echo "-- gate q: waiting list (the board loses nothing — no over-cap shown set, no demotion into the void, SPEC INV-206) --"
if ! python3 "$GUARDRAILS/check-board.py"; then
  fail=1
fi

echo ""
echo "-- gate r: authority anchor (a decision recorded as the person's names its exchange, SPEC INV-207) --"
if ! python3 "$GUARDRAILS/check-authority-anchor.py"; then
  fail=1
fi

echo ""
echo "-- gate s: skill review (a substantive skill change carries its skill-creator review record, SPEC INV-208) --"
if ! "$GUARDRAILS/check-skill-review.sh"; then
  fail=1
fi

echo ""
echo "-- gate t: doc rotation (the pack's split-and-rotated docs lose nothing — every rotated row is findable in its archive and every archive is named in a manifest line, SPEC INV-209) --"
if ! python3 "$GUARDRAILS/check-doc-rotation.py"; then
  fail=1
fi

echo ""
echo "-- gate m: config health (installed hooks match guardrails/ source, SPEC INV-175) --"
if ! "$GUARDRAILS/check-config-health.sh"; then
  fail=1
fi

echo ""
echo "-- gate k: compaction freeze (guarded docs' anchor map / markers / numbers unchanged, 2.0) --"
if ! "$GUARDRAILS/check-freeze.sh"; then
  fail=1
fi

echo ""
echo "-- gate n: the earned message (an agent's inbox deposit names its birth, SPEC INV-189) --"
# Report-only at push (the owner's word, 2026-08-07 11:19): a deposit is recorded on arrival and
# never blocks a push. The check's judging moment is the intake sweep, which declines an unearned
# deposit at the door. Here it prints what the sweep will meet and the push proceeds either way.
if [ -f "$GUARDRAILS/check-earned-message.py" ] && [ -d "$REPO_ROOT/inbox" ]; then
  python3 "$GUARDRAILS/check-earned-message.py" "$REPO_ROOT/inbox" || \
    echo "   (deposits above await the intake sweep; a deposit never blocks a push)"
else
  echo "   (no inbox in this tree — the gate stands down by name)"
fi

# The named-reference presence nets (SPEC INV-239) take NO push-gate letter and are NOT invoked here:
# they RIDE THE SUITE (gate b), the same placement the far-tier report-shape check takes. Their suite
# tests run each net against the real tree and assert the expected result, so a real violation reds
# the suite and gate b already blocks this push. A suite-riding check carries no gate letter, so the
# letter-counting meta-guards (INV-210, INV-212) need not see it and no gate-red-proofs / ci-mirror
# entry is owed.

echo ""
echo "-- gate h: the four host checks (this repo attached as its own first host, SPEC INV-97) --"
for hostcheck in completeness tests_present traces_to_spec conflicts; do
  if ! python3 "$REPO_ROOT/scaffold/guardrails/check_${hostcheck}.py" --base origin/main; then
    fail=1
  fi
done

echo ""
echo "-- gate u: CI mirror parity (every local gate is mirrored in CI or a declared carve-out, SPEC INV-210) --"
if ! "$GUARDRAILS/check-ci-mirror.sh"; then
  fail=1
fi

echo ""
echo "-- gate v: judges listed (every wired chat judge is referenced in the installed settings.json, SPEC INV-211) --"
if ! python3 "$GUARDRAILS/check-judge-listed.py"; then
  fail=1
fi

echo ""
echo "-- gate w: every gate can fail (every gate in this chain carries a known-red proof, SPEC INV-212) --"
if ! python3 "$GUARDRAILS/check-every-gate-can-fail.py"; then
  fail=1
fi

echo ""
echo "-- gate x: generated index (the committed index equals a fresh build off the body; body and index agree; an empty body reds by name, SPEC INV-258/INV-259/INV-218) --"
if ! python3 "$GUARDRAILS/check-index-generated.py" "$REPO_ROOT/PRODUCT_SPEC.md" "$REPO_ROOT/PRODUCT_SPEC.index.md"; then
  fail=1
fi

echo ""
echo "-- gate y: agent card (a live-spec host tree carries its .live-spec/agent.md card, SPEC INV-219) --"
if ! python3 "$GUARDRAILS/check-agent-card.py"; then
  fail=1
fi

echo ""
echo "-- gate aa: doc findings bound (no live document above its recorded finding count; a cleared document stays at zero, SPEC INV-301) --"
if ! python3 "$GUARDRAILS/check-doc-findings-bound.py"; then
  fail=1
fi

echo ""
echo "-- gate ad: published tree counts (every count this repository publishes about its own tree matches the tree, and the reproduction command beside it returns the published number, SPEC INV-305) --"
if ! python3 "$GUARDRAILS/check-tree-counts.py"; then
  fail=1
fi

echo ""
echo "-- gate ae: named checks (the registry says what each runnable file a skill body names is, SPEC INV-306) --"
if ! python3 "$GUARDRAILS/check-named-checks.py"; then
  fail=1
fi

echo ""
echo "-- gate af: gate device manifest (guardrails/gates-manifest.json joins every gate's script, red proof and CI-mirror status from pre-push, gate-red-proofs.json and ci-mirror.json; it reds where a fresh build differs from the committed file, or where a gates.yml step's law sentence differs from the gate's own, SPEC INV-210/INV-212) --"
if ! python3 "$GUARDRAILS/check-gates-manifest.py"; then
  fail=1
fi

echo ""
if [ "$fail" -ne 0 ]; then
  echo "PUSH BLOCKED — one or more gates above failed. Fix them and try again."
  exit 1
fi

echo "All gates green — push allowed."
exit 0

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# check-tests.sh — gate (b) of the push gate: the test suite must be fully green.
#
# This also covers gate (c), anchor ownership: tests/test_traceability.py already
# asserts every spec anchor is owned by exactly one architecture node
# (TestArchitecture::test_architecture_owns_every_anchor_once). A green suite run
# proves both gates in one pass — no separate anchor-ownership check exists here.
#
# Scoped runs (SPEC INV-45, ROADMAP row 362): when env SCOPED_TEST_FILES is non-empty
# (newline-separated test file paths), only those files run — the reach map's SCOPED verdict
# already proved this set covers the diff.
#
# Suite wall-time budget (SPEC INV-41, INV-164, ROADMAP row 361): a green FULL default run (the
# real tests dir, no SCOPED_TEST_FILES, no LIVE_SPEC_SCRATCH) is followed by
# guardrails/check-suite-budget.sh reading this run's own captured log — a budget red makes this
# gate red too. A scoped or scratch run stands the budget check down by name: it is not the run
# the stated budget describes.
#
# Usage: check-tests.sh [tests-dir]
#   tests-dir defaults to "tests" (relative to the repo root, or an absolute path
#   for testing this gate against a scratch fixture without touching the real suite)
#   SCOPED_TEST_FILES (env, optional): newline-separated test file paths — run exactly these
#   instead of the whole tests-dir.
#
# An explicit tests-dir names its OWN repo root as its parent directory, never the ambient
# cwd's repo (tests/test_guardrails.py::TestGateB_Tests' scratch runs are the caller this
# protects): a caller that launches this script from inside the real, judged tree while
# pointing it at a scratch copy elsewhere must not have this script `cd` back into that judged
# tree and hand it, as the nested pytest process's inherited cwd, to every test the scratch
# copy runs — the same class of defect d747bcd fixed for docs/PROGRESS.md, one layer down.

set -euo pipefail

# A hook runs with git's own environment exported, and an inherited GIT_DIR outranks any
# `-C` a test passes: a fixture that builds its own little repository would commit into
# the repository being pushed instead. The suite starts from a clean git environment.
unset GIT_DIR GIT_WORK_TREE GIT_INDEX_FILE GIT_OBJECT_DIRECTORY \
      GIT_ALTERNATE_OBJECT_DIRECTORIES GIT_COMMON_DIR GIT_QUARANTINE_PATH \
      GIT_PREFIX GIT_NAMESPACE

if [ -n "${1:-}" ]; then
  TESTS_DIR="$1"
  REPO_ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "$TESTS_DIR")" && pwd)"
else
  REPO_ROOT="$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel 2>/dev/null || pwd)"
  TESTS_DIR="tests"
fi
cd "$REPO_ROOT"

LOG="$(mktemp "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/livespec-test-suite-log.XXXXXX")"
cleanup() { rm -f "$LOG"; }
trap cleanup EXIT

# The runner MUST match the CI mirror's (.github/workflows/gates.yml runs `python3 -m pytest -q`);
# the two nets share one runner or the local net is weaker than the second one (SPEC M-5, M-154);
# unittest discover cannot collect the plain-function pytest-style tests (fixtures like monkeypatch/
# tmp_path), so it silently under-runs and false-greens — the exact hole that let a red reach CI.
if [ -n "${SCOPED_TEST_FILES:-}" ]; then
  scoped_count=0
  scoped_list=()
  while IFS= read -r t; do
    [ -z "$t" ] && continue
    scoped_list+=("$t")
    scoped_count=$((scoped_count + 1))
  done <<< "$SCOPED_TEST_FILES"

  set +e
  python3 -m pytest -q "${scoped_list[@]}" 2>&1 | tee "$LOG"
  status="${PIPESTATUS[0]}"
  set -e

  if [ "$status" -eq 0 ]; then
    echo "OK (tests): scoped suite green ($scoped_count files, reach-scoped per SPEC INV-45)."
    echo "suite budget: stands down by name (scoped or scratch run)"
    exit 0
  else
    echo "FAIL (tests): scoped suite is not green ($scoped_count files)."
    echo "  Fix: run 'python3 -m pytest -q' on the scoped files and repair the failing test(s)."
    exit 1
  fi
fi

set +e
python3 -m pytest -q "$TESTS_DIR" 2>&1 | tee "$LOG"
status="${PIPESTATUS[0]}"
set -e

if [ "$status" -ne 0 ]; then
  echo "FAIL (tests): suite is not green ($TESTS_DIR)."
  echo "  Fix: run 'python3 -m pytest -q tests' and repair the failing test(s) before pushing."
  exit 1
fi

echo "OK (tests): suite green ($TESTS_DIR) — also covers anchor ownership (gate c)."

if [ "$TESTS_DIR" = "tests" ] && [ -z "${LIVE_SPEC_SCRATCH:-}" ]; then
  if ! "$REPO_ROOT/guardrails/check-suite-budget.sh" "$LOG"; then
    exit 1
  fi
else
  echo "suite budget: stands down by name (scoped or scratch run)"
fi

exit 0

# gates.yml — the CI mirror of the push gate (SPEC M-5, ROADMAP row 14).
# Same checks, one source of truth: CI runs the SAME scripts the local pre-push hook
# runs — it never redefines them. This is the SECOND net: the local reach map
# (SPEC INV-45) is a developer-latency optimization; the CI net always runs the full set.
name: gates
on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  pull_request:

jobs:
  gates:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    env:
      TZ: Asia/Jerusalem   # gate (a) wants a today-dated prover record; "today" is the author's day, not UTC's
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v5
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0    # gate (a)'s freshness rule reads commit history (record vs PRODUCT_SPEC.md)
      - uses: actions/setup-python@v6
...
          base="${{ github.event.before }}"
          if [ -z "$base" ] || ! git cat-file -e "${base}^{commit}" 2>/dev/null; then
            git fetch -q origin main 2>/dev/null || true
            base="origin/main"
          fi
          if ! git cat-file -e "${base}^{commit}" 2>/dev/null; then base="HEAD~1"; fi
          for c in completeness tests_present traces_to_spec conflicts; do
            python3 scaffold/guardrails/check_${c}.py --base "$base"
          done
      - name: "gate n — the earned message (an agent's inbox deposit names its birth, SPEC INV-189)"
        if: ${{ !cancelled() }}
        run: |
          # Report-only (the owner's word, 2026-08-07 11:19): a deposit never blocks a push;
          # the intake sweep is the judging moment.
          if [ -d inbox ]; then
            python3 guardrails/check-earned-message.py inbox || \
              echo "deposits above await the intake sweep; a deposit never blocks a push"
          else
            echo "no inbox in this checkout — the gate stands down by name"
          fi
      # The named-reference presence nets (SPEC INV-239) take NO push-gate letter: they RIDE THE SUITE
      # (the pytest step, gate b), the same placement the far-tier report-shape check takes, so they
      # need no separate CI step here and no ci-mirror carve-out — a suite-riding check carries no gate
      # letter for the mirror to track.
      - name: "gate u — CI mirror parity (every local gate is mirrored in CI or a declared carve-out, SPEC INV-210)"
        if: ${{ !cancelled() }}
        run: guardrails/check-ci-mirror.sh
      - name: "gate w — every gate can fail (every gate in this chain carries a known-red proof, SPEC INV-212)"
        if: ${{ !cancelled() }}
        run: python3 guardrails/check-every-gate-can-fail.py
      - name: "gate x — generated index (the committed index equals a fresh build off the body; body and index agree; an empty body reds by name, SPEC INV-258/INV-259/INV-218)"
        if: ${{ !cancelled() }}
        run: python3 guardrails/check-index-generated.py PRODUCT_SPEC.md PRODUCT_SPEC.index.md
      - name: "gate y — agent card (a live-spec host tree carries its .live-spec/agent.md card, SPEC INV-219)"
        if: ${{ !cancelled() }}
        run: python3 guardrails/check-agent-card.py
      - name: "gate aa — doc findings bound (no live document above its recorded finding count; a cleared document stays at zero, SPEC INV-301)"
        if: ${{ !cancelled() }}
        # The record arm reads the record against the state the remote already holds (SPEC R302.12).
        # github.event.before is the pre-push SHA on a push; on a PR it is empty and the arm falls back
        # to origin/main, which the fetch-depth-0 checkout above carries.
        env:
          LIVE_SPEC_DIFF_BASE: ${{ github.event.before }}
        run: python3 guardrails/check-doc-findings-bound.py
      - name: "gate ad — published tree counts (every count this repository publishes about its own tree matches the tree, and the reproduction command beside it returns the published number, SPEC INV-305)"
        if: ${{ !cancelled() }}
        run: python3 guardrails/check-tree-counts.py
      - name: "gate ae — named checks (the registry says what each runnable file a skill body names is, SPEC INV-306)"
        if: ${{ !cancelled() }}
        run: python3 guardrails/check-named-checks.py
      - name: "gate af — gate device manifest (guardrails/gates-manifest.json joins every gate's script, red proof and CI-mirror status from pre-push, gate-red-proofs.json and ci-mirror.json; it reds where a fresh build differs from the committed file, or where a gates.yml step's law sentence differs from the gate's own, SPEC INV-210/INV-212)"
        if: ${{ !cancelled() }}
        run: python3 guardrails/check-gates-manifest.py

# gates.yml — the CI mirror of the push gate (SPEC M-5, ROADMAP row 14).
# Same checks, one source of truth: CI runs the SAME scripts the local pre-push hook
# runs — it never redefines them. This is the SECOND net: the local reach map
# (SPEC INV-45) is a developer-latency optimization; the CI net always runs the full set.
name: gates
on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  pull_request:

jobs:
  gates:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    env:
      TZ: Asia/Jerusalem   # gate (a) wants a today-dated prover record; "today" is the author's day, not UTC's
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v5
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0    # gate (a)'s freshness rule reads commit history (record vs PRODUCT_SPEC.md)
      - uses: actions/setup-python@v6
        with:
          python-version: "3.12"
      - name: "install pytest"
        run: pip install pytest pyyaml
      # The external canon, pinned. Before this step existed the suite ran with no clone,
      # so every assertion that reads the externalized product-prover skipped on every CI
      # run forever, and CI claimed a green it had not earned (ROADMAP row 622 territory;
      # the same fork the emergency branch reached from the other side). The pack now
      # INSTALLS the canon rather than pretending to prove it: --ref names the exact commit
      # the pack's assertions are written against, and --expect-commit verifies the checkout
      # landed there, so a moved tag or branch cannot change what CI proves. Moving the pin
      # is a deliberate pack change; tests/test_prover_adapter_contract.py holds its shape.
      - name: "install the external product-prover canon (pinned, gate b's evidence)"
        run: >-
          scripts/install-external-skills.sh
          --ref 540914d740e4f6178d1a69f324c43a0ae871e066
          --expect-commit 540914d740e4f6178d1a69f324c43a0ae871e066
      - name: "test suite (gate b, full — the reach map stays local)"
        if: ${{ !cancelled() }}
        run: python3 -m pytest -q
      - name: "gate a — fresh prover record for today (one record per push: the re-check of the spec and the architecture, and the adversarial read of the pushed range, SPEC M-6/INV-116/INV-304)"
        if: ${{ !cancelled() }}
        # LIVE_SPEC_DIFF_BASE lets the script judge the inbox-only carve-out (row 269,
        # SPEC M-6/INV-112): a push whose diff is exactly one new inbox/ file owes no
        # fresh record. The same base carries the range arm, which reads the pushed delta
        # against the state the remote already holds. github.event.before is the pre-push
        # SHA on a push; on a PR it is empty and the script falls back to origin/main,
        # which the fetch-depth-0 checkout above carries.
        env:
          LIVE_SPEC_DIFF_BASE: ${{ github.event.before }}
        run: guardrails/check-prover-record.sh --push
      - name: "gate d — TEST_MATRIX.md generated Reference agrees with the body (SPEC INV-273/INV-218)"
        if: ${{ !cancelled() }}
        run: python3 guardrails/check-matrix-reference.py TEST_MATRIX.md TEST_MATRIX.index.md
      - name: "gate g — pin drift"
        if: ${{ !cancelled() }}
        run: guardrails/check-pin-drift.sh
      - name: "gate f — skill loadability"
        if: ${{ !cancelled() }}
        run: guardrails/check-skill-loadability.sh
      - name: "gate e — prototype fence"
        if: ${{ !cancelled() }}
        run: guardrails/check-prototype-fence.sh
      - name: "gate i — shipped-language (no owner name or stray Cyrillic in the shipped set, SPEC INV-120)"
        if: ${{ !cancelled() }}
        run: guardrails/check-shipped-language.sh
      - name: "gate j — no broad browser-kill (cleanup targets the test resource only, SPEC INV-162)"
        if: ${{ !cancelled() }}
        run: guardrails/check-broad-kill.sh
      - name: "gate l — muted browser launch (every browser-driving script launches muted, SPEC INV-157)"
        if: ${{ !cancelled() }}
        run: guardrails/check-muted-launch.sh
      - name: "gate o — cleanup notice (every cleanup path that ends a process says what it ended, SPEC INV-204)"
        if: ${{ !cancelled() }}
        run: guardrails/check-cleanup-notice.sh
      - name: "gate p — touchpoint kind (a surface speaks only the kind its touchpoint affords, SPEC INV-205)"
        if: ${{ !cancelled() }}
        run: python3 guardrails/check-touchpoint-kind.py
      - name: "gate q — waiting list (the board loses nothing — no over-cap shown set, no demotion into the void, SPEC INV-206)"
        if: ${{ !cancelled() }}
        run: python3 guardrails/check-board.py
      - name: "gate r — authority anchor (a decision recorded as the person's names its exchange, SPEC INV-207)"
        if: ${{ !cancelled() }}
        run: python3 guardrails/check-authority-anchor.py
      - name: "gate s — skill review (a substantive skill change carries its skill-creator review record, SPEC INV-208)"
        if: ${{ !cancelled() }}
        # LIVE_SPEC_DIFF_BASE lets the gate read the push range (the same base as gate a); on a PR it
        # is empty and the gate falls back to origin/main.
        env:
          LIVE_SPEC_DIFF_BASE: ${{ github.event.before }}
        run: guardrails/check-skill-review.sh
      - name: "gate t — doc rotation (the pack's split-and-rotated docs lose nothing — every rotated row is findable in its archive and every archive is named in a manifest line, SPEC INV-209)"
        if: ${{ !cancelled() }}
        run: python3 guardrails/check-doc-rotation.py
      - name: "gate h — the four host checks (this repo attached as its own first host, SPEC INV-97)"
        if: ${{ !cancelled() }}
        # The base ladder mirrors gate a: github.event.before on a push, else a fetched origin/main,
        # else HEAD~1 — so the host checks compare against a ref that exists on any CI checkout.
        run: |
          base="${{ github.event.before }}"
          if [ -z "$base" ] || ! git cat-file -e "${base}^{commit}" 2>/dev/null; then
            git fetch -q origin main 2>/dev/null || true
            base="origin/main"
          fi
          if ! git cat-file -e "${base}^{commit}" 2>/dev/null; then base="HEAD~1"; fi
          for c in completeness tests_present traces_to_spec conflicts; do
            python3 scaffold/guardrails/check_${c}.py --base "$base"
          done
      - name: "gate n — the earned message (an agent's inbox deposit names its birth, SPEC INV-189)"
        if: ${{ !cancelled() }}
        run: |
          # Report-only (the owner's word, 2026-08-07 11:19): a deposit never blocks a push;
          # the intake sweep is the judging moment.
          if [ -d inbox ]; then
            python3 guardrails/check-earned-message.py inbox || \
              echo "deposits above await the intake sweep; a deposit never blocks a push"
          else
            echo "no inbox in this checkout — the gate stands down by name"
          fi
      # The named-reference presence nets (SPEC INV-239) take NO push-gate letter: they RIDE THE SUITE
      # (the pytest step, gate b), the same placement the far-tier report-shape check takes, so they
      # need no separate CI step here and no ci-mirror carve-out — a suite-riding check carries no gate
      # letter for the mirror to track.
      - name: "gate u — CI mirror parity (every local gate is mirrored in CI or a declared carve-out, SPEC INV-210)"
        if: ${{ !cancelled() }}
        run: guardrails/check-ci-mirror.sh
      - name: "gate w — every gate can fail (every gate in this chain carries a known-red proof, SPEC INV-212)"
        if: ${{ !cancelled() }}
        run: python3 guardrails/check-every-gate-can-fail.py
      - name: "gate x — generated index (the committed index equals a fresh build off the body; body and index agree; an empty body reds by name, SPEC INV-258/INV-259/INV-218)"
        if: ${{ !cancelled() }}
        run: python3 guardrails/check-index-generated.py PRODUCT_SPEC.md PRODUCT_SPEC.index.md
      - name: "gate y — agent card (a live-spec host tree carries its .live-spec/agent.md card, SPEC INV-219)"
        if: ${{ !cancelled() }}
        run: python3 guardrails/check-agent-card.py
      - name: "gate aa — doc findings bound (no live document above its recorded finding count; a cleared document stays at zero, SPEC INV-301)"
        if: ${{ !cancelled() }}
        # The record arm reads the record against the state the remote already holds (SPEC R302.12).
        # github.event.before is the pre-push SHA on a push; on a PR it is empty and the arm falls back
        # to origin/main, which the fetch-depth-0 checkout above carries.
        env:
          LIVE_SPEC_DIFF_BASE: ${{ github.event.before }}
        run: python3 guardrails/check-doc-findings-bound.py
      - name: "gate ad — published tree counts (every count this repository publishes about its own tree matches the tree, and the reproduction command beside it returns the published number, SPEC INV-305)"
        if: ${{ !cancelled() }}
        run: python3 guardrails/check-tree-counts.py
      - name: "gate ae — named checks (the registry says what each runnable file a skill body names is, SPEC INV-306)"
        if: ${{ !cancelled() }}
        run: python3 guardrails/check-named-checks.py
      - name: "gate af — gate device manifest (guardrails/gates-manifest.json joins every gate's script, red proof and CI-mirror status from pre-push, gate-red-proofs.json and ci-mirror.json; it reds where a fresh build differs from the committed file, or where a gates.yml step's law sentence differs from the gate's own, SPEC INV-210/INV-212)"
        if: ${{ !cancelled() }}
        run: python3 guardrails/check-gates-manifest.py
